newsitem.title: USA: USWC gasoline prices rise on tight supply, buying.
newsitem.headline: USWC gasoline prices rise on tight supply, buying.

text.p: Offers for spot barrels of U.S. West Coast gasoline rose late Thursday, driven by tight regional supply and increased demand from refiners, brokers said.

"If it hadn't been for (a lower) Merc, we would have been over 80 cents a gallon," one broker said, noting major refiners resumed bidding after the New York Mercantile Exchanged (Merc) halted a week-long slide two days ago.
But supplies remained tight, with traders noting the American Petroleum Institute (API) reported West Coast gasoline off 554,000 barrels last week.
Refineries, including Mobil, Ultramar and Unocal, also needed to buy ahead of this week's pipeline scheduling deadlines, traders said.
One trader said Exxon's xxx,000 barrel-per-day refinery in northern California began the restart of several and was expected to be completely on line by mid-March.
CARB gasoline in Los Angeles rose one cent a gallon to 74/75 cents, after a deal was struck at 74.50 cents today.
Offers for conventioal L.A. gasoline rose one penny to 71 cents, tracking perceptions of tightness in California.
San Francisco CARB gasoline was done at 71.50 cents, within yesterday's ranges, traders said.
Among distillates, CARB diesel was done at 73 cents, bringing offers up one cent to 74 cents a gallon.
